understand.concept: Catch specific exceptions before broader ones. Java multi-catch uses a vertical bar for alternatives that share one recovery path. Do not catch Exception merely to silence errors; recover only when the program can take a useful action.
understand.whyItMatters: Multiple Exceptions and Multi-Catch helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain. It connects core language knowledge with realistic programming tasks.

explain.narrative:
## Multiple Exceptions and Multi-Catch

Catch specific exceptions before broader ones. Java multi-catch uses a vertical bar for alternatives that share one recovery path. Do not catch Exception merely to silence errors; recover only when the program can take a useful action.

## Applying the concept

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that directly supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failure cases and state assumptions clearly.

## Verification checklist

- Compile with JDK 21.
- Predict the output before running.
- Test normal, boundary and invalid inputs where relevant.
- Check resource cleanup and error handling.
- Prefer explicit types and focused methods.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try { System.out.println(Integer.parseInt("25")); } catch (NumberFormatException ex) { System.out.println("Not a number"); } } }

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try { Integer.parseInt("x"); } catch (NumberFormatException | NullPointerException ex) { System.out.println("Input conversion failed"); } } }
examples.explanation: Uses multi-catch for two unrelated exceptions with the same recovery action.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try { int[] a = {1, 2}; System.out.println(a[4]); } catch (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException ex) { System.out.println("Index outside array"); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows a specific exception handler for an invalid array index.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try { throw new java.io.IOException("disk unavailable"); } catch (java.io.IOException ex) { System.out.println(ex.getMessage()); } } }
examples.explanation: Handles a checked IOException and retains its diagnostic message.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try { Integer.parseInt("bad"); } catch (NumberFormatException ex) { System.out.println(ex.getClass().getSimpleName()); } catch (RuntimeException ex) { System.out.println("Other runtime failure"); } } }
examples.explanation: Orders a specific catch before a broader RuntimeException catch.
